arxiv-2006-00356.title: Critical Assessment of Transfer Learning for Medical Image Segmentation with Fully Convolutional Neural Networks
arxiv-2006-00356.creator: Davood Karimi, Simon K. Warfield, Ali Gholipour
arxiv-2006-00356.description: Abstract Transfer learning is widely used for training machine learning models. Here, we study the role of transfer learning for training fully convolutional networks (FCNs) for medical image segmentation. Our experiments show that although transfer learning reduces the training time on the target task, the improvement in segmentation accuracy is highly task/data-dependent.

arxiv-2109-12142.title: Periodicity in Cryptocurrency Volatility and Liquidity Thanks: We are grateful to Tim Bollerslev, Chris Cashwell, and Mark Ettinger for many useful and constructive comments and to Emily Dyckman for proofreading the article. Thanks: Disclosure: The first and second authors have served as compensated
arxiv-2109-12142.creator: Peter Reinhard Hansen Chan Kim Wade Kimbrough
arxiv-2109-12142.description: Abstract We study recurrent patterns in volatility and volume for major cryptocurrencies, Bitcoin and Ether, using data from two centralized exchanges (Coinbase Pro and Binance) and a decentralized exchange (Uniswap V2). We find systematic patterns in both volatility and volume across day-of-the-week, hour-of-the-day, and within the hour.

arxiv-2209-06261.title: Real2Sim2Real Transfer for Control of Cable-driven Robots via a Differentiable Physics Engine
arxiv-2209-06261.creator: Kun Wang, William R. Johnson III, Shiyang Lu, Xiaonan Huang, Joran Booth, Rebecca Kramer-Bottiglio, Mridul Aanjaneya, Kostas Bekris
arxiv-2209-06261.description: Abstract Tensegrity robots, composed of rigid rods and flexible cables, exhibit high strength-to-weight ratios and significant deformations, which enable them to navigate unstructured terrains and survive harsh impacts. They are hard to control, however, due to high dimensionality, complex dynamics, and a coupled architecture.

arxiv-2305-10209.title: Measurement-induced multipartite-entanglement regimes in collective spin systems
arxiv-2305-10209.creator: Pablo M. Poggi, Manuel H. Muñoz-Arias
arxiv-2305-10209.description: Abstract We study the competing effects of collective generalized measurements and interaction-induced scrambling in the dynamics of an ensemble of spin- 1 / 2 1/2 particles at the level of quantum trajectories. This setup can be considered as analogous to the one leading to measurement-induced transitions in quantum circuits.

arxiv-2309-12939.title: Bright beacons? ALMA non-detection of a supposedly bright [OI] 63- μ \mu m line in a redshift-6 dusty galaxy Facilities: ALMA, APEX
arxiv-2309-12939.creator: Matus Rybak, L. Lemsom, A. Lundgren, J. Zavala, J. A. Hodge, C. de Breuck, C. M. Casey, R. Decarli, K. Torstensson, J. L. Wardlow, P. P. van der Werf
arxiv-2309-12939.description: Abstract We report a non-detection of the [O I] 63- μ \mu m emission line from the z = 6.03 z=6.03 galaxy G09.83808 using ALMA Band 9 observations, refuting the previously claimed detection with APEX by [ 10 ] ; the new upper limit on the [O I] 63- μ \mu m flux is almost 20-times lower.

arxiv-2311-13801.title: A selective review of recent developments in spatially variable gene detection for spatial transcriptomics
arxiv-2311-13801.creator: Sikta Das Adhikari, Jiaxin Yang, Jianrong Wang, Yuehua Cui
arxiv-2311-13801.description: Abstract With the emergence of advanced spatial transcriptomic technologies, there has been a surge in research papers dedicated to analyzing spatial transcriptomics data, resulting in significant contributions to our understanding of biology. The initial stage of downstream analysis of spatial transcriptomic data has centered on identifying spatially variable genes (SVGs) or genes expressed with specific spatial patterns across the tissue.

arxiv-2401-06685.title: A counterexample to the coarse Menger conjecture
arxiv-2401-06685.creator: Tung Nguyen, Alex Scott, Paul Seymour
arxiv-2401-06685.description: A 2024 arXiv research paper by Tung Nguyen, Alex Scott, Paul Seymour. Menger’s well-known theorem from 1927 characterizes when it is possible to find k k vertex-disjoint paths between two sets of vertices in a graph G G . Recently, Georgakopoulos and Papasoglu and, independently, Albrechtsen, Huynh, Jacobs, Knappe and Wollan conjectured a coarse analogue of Menger’s theorem, when the k k paths are required to be pairwise at some distance at least d d .

arxiv-2401-11267.title: Charge transfer transitions and circular magnetooptics in ferrites
arxiv-2401-11267.creator: A.S. Moskvin
arxiv-2401-11267.description: A 2024 arXiv research paper by A.S. Moskvin. The concept of charge-transfer (CT) transitions in ferrites is based on the cluster approach and takes into account the relevant interactions as the low-symmetry crystal field, spin-orbital, Zeeman, exchange and exchange-relativistic interactions. For all its simplicity, this concept yield a reliable qualitative and quantitative microscopic explanation of spectral, concentration, temperature, and field dependences of optic and magneto-optic properties ranging from the isotropic absorption as well as the optic anisotropy to the circular magneto-optics.

arxiv-2406-01445.title: Tunably-polarized driving light controls the phase diagram of 1D quasicrystals and 2D quantum Hall matter
arxiv-2406-01445.creator: Yifei Bai, David M. Weld
arxiv-2406-01445.description: Abstract The well-known mapping between 1D quasiperiodic systems and 2D integer quantum Hall matter can also be applied in the presence of driving. Here we explore the effect of time-varying electric fields on the transport properties and phase diagram of Harper-Hofstadter materials.

arxiv-2504-19289.title: Marine Snow Removal Using Internally Generated Pseudo Ground Truth Thanks: This work is supported by EPSRC IAA, University of Bristol, and EPSRC ECR (EP/Y002490/1).
arxiv-2504-19289.creator: Alexandra Malyugina, Guoxi Huang, Eduardo Ruiz, Benjamin Leslie, Nantheera Anantrasirichai
arxiv-2504-19289.description: Abstract Underwater videos often suffer from degraded quality due to light absorption, scattering, and various noise sources. Among these, marine snow—suspended organic particles appearing as bright spots or noise—significantly impacts machine vision tasks, particularly those involving feature matching. Existing methods for removing marine snow are ineffective due to the lack of paired training data.

arxiv-2510-02181.title: EvolveCaptions: Empowering DHH Users Through Real-Time Collaborative Captioning CCS: Human-centered computing Accessibility systems and tools
arxiv-2510-02181.creator: Liang-Yuan Wu, Dhruv Jain
arxiv-2510-02181.description: Abstract . Automatic Speech Recognition (ASR) systems often fail to accurately transcribe speech from Deaf and Hard of Hearing (DHH) individuals, especially during real-time conversations. Existing personalization approaches typically require extensive pre-recorded data and place the burden of adaptation on the DHH speaker. We present EvolveCaptions, a real-time, collaborative ASR adaptation system that supports in-situ personalization with minimal effort.

arxiv-2601-15346.title: Conjectures on Sums of Consecutive Primes
arxiv-2601-15346.creator: Edwige Tolla
arxiv-2601-15346.description: A 2026 arXiv research paper by Edwige Tolla. We study additive properties of consecutive prime numbers and the primality of the sums they generate. For a given prime number p n p_{n} , we consider the sums S k ​ ( p n ) = p n + p n + 1 + ⋯ + p n + k − 1 , S_{k}(p_{n})=p_{n}+p_{n+1}+\cdots+p_{n+k-1}, where k ≥ 3 k\geq 3 is an odd integer.
